newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 1.1 pct wk March 8 -Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 1.1 pct wk March 8 -Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 1.1 percent in the first week of fiscal March versus February, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.

The index rose 8.6 percent compared to the same month a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales also jumped 8.6 percent in the week ended March 8 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.
"Retailers reported a seasonal tone to merchandise trends with, for instance, horticultural lines doing well at discount stores," the report said.
Soft lines continued to drive sales at department stores, and discounters saw a pickup in apparel and accessories, such as children's wear and footwear, it said.
The aggregate sales growth target for March, a measure of retailers' plans, hit 8.0 percent, well above the 6.0-percent increase in February, the report said.
"The increase is entirely the result of expected sales gains at national department stores and discounters," the report said.
But regional department store projections are about the same as they were in February, indicating modest growth in this sector, it said.
